console.description: The application's own commands, granted to the one origin the console is served from and to nothing else. Tauri denies every application command to remote content unless a capability names its origin (tauri 2.11.5, src/webview/mod.rs:1819-1850), so without this the seller would press a button and read a permission error. The url here must equal control_plane::DEFAULT_BASE_URL; the_capability_grants_the_origin_this_build_uses asserts it, because a cutover that moved the constant and the content-security policy and forgot this file would build clean, ship, and refuse every command at run time. These seven are granted LOCALLY as well as remotely, because `local` defaults to true and this file does not set it false. That is deliberate rather than an oversight: with TAM_CONTROL_PLANE pointing at the vite dev server the window is local content, `is_local_url` answers true, and without the local grant every command would be refused in development while working in production — the worst way round. Nothing in the marketplace login windows is granted, here or anywhere: their window label is not main.

default.description: The console window's local grants, and only it. The login webview is absent from every capability, so no command resolves for it, and that absence is the whole fence. It is not that a marketplace page has no bridge: Tauri injects the IPC internals into every webview it creates regardless of URL (tauri 2.11.5, src/manager/webview.rs:166-200), and app.withGlobalTauri adds window.__TAURI__ on top of them. What a page at a marketplace origin lacks is permission, because its window label is not main and nothing here grants it anything. This capability carries no remote block, so nothing in it reaches remote content: the plugin and core permissions here are the ones the bundled fallback page needs, and the application's own console commands are granted separately in console.json, to one named origin and to local content as well — local because the development override serves the console from the vite origin, where the window is local content and a remote-only grant would refuse every command in development. The one exception is allow-retry-console, which is here because the page that calls it is the bundled fallback shown when the control plane cannot be reached: that page runs at the Tauri origin, where the console never does, and it can reach nothing on its own. Splitting them is what stops a widening of the console grant silently widening the updater's. The updater's own grant has since moved out of this file entirely, to updater.json, because tauri-plugin-updater is no longer a dependency of the Android build and a capability naming a permission whose plugin is absent fails the build rather than being ignored: `Permission updater:default not found`. That file carries the platform list this one deliberately does not. One thing about that fence reads differently on Android and is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered: there is one Activity, so a marketplace login cannot have a window of its own and instead replaces the console inside window main — the very label every capability here names. What refuses a marketplace page there is therefore not the absent label but the per-invoke remote-origin check (tauri 2.11.5, src/webview/mod.rs), tested against the one origin console.json grants. That check is only as good as the origin list, which is what control_plane::the_capability_grants_the_origin_this_build_uses asserts is exactly one entry and equal to DEFAULT_BASE_URL.

opener.description: Handing one marketplace URL to the browser the seller already uses, and nothing else. Its own file rather than a line in default.json because it needs a remote block and that file deliberately carries none: adding one there would extend core:event, core:window, os:allow-hostname and allow-retry-console to the control plane's origin as a side effect of this change. The url must equal the one console.json names and control_plane::DEFAULT_BASE_URL, for the reason console.json states; web/src/lib/desktop.test.ts asserts the two capability files agree. Granted locally as well, because `local` defaults to true and the development override serves the console from the vite origin, where the window is local content. No platforms list, unlike updater.json: the plugin declares an Android implementation and Android is the platform this is most needed on, where the webview has no second window and a marketplace link replaces the console itself. allow-open-url rather than opener:default, which also carries open-path and reveal-item-in-dir — a filesystem surface, and one this grants to a remote origin. The scope is not decoration on that permission but the half that makes it work: allow-open-url arrives with an empty allow list, and tauri-plugin-opener 2.5.5 answers is_url_allowed with `self.allowed.iter().any(..)` (src/scope.rs), so the bare permission refuses every url. https only, which is narrower than the plugin's own allow-default-urls set: it leaves out mailto:, tel: and plaintext http:, and every link this console opens — a marketplace listing url and a catalogue homepage — is https. The founder authorised `opener:allow-open-url`; the scope narrower than upstream's default was measured and accepted on 2026-09-06, so widening it back to opener:default or to allow-default-urls is a new decision rather than a fix. The window is main, so the marketplace login webviews keep having no grant to anything, which is the fence default.json describes.

updater.description: The updater's grant, on the platforms that have an updater. Split out of default.json rather than left beside the other window grants, because tauri-plugin-updater is a desktop-only dependency: it declares platforms.support.android.level = "none" in its own manifest, lib.rs registers it under #[cfg(desktop)], and its Cargo entry is scoped to cfg(not(any(target_os = "android", target_os = "ios"))). A capability that names a permission whose plugin is not a dependency of the target being built is a build failure and not a silent no-op — the Android build stops with `Permission updater:default not found` — so the platform list below is what makes the split work rather than decoration on it. The window is main because that is the only window this application creates and the only one the updater's own commands are reached from; the login webview is absent from every capability, here as everywhere.
